speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you have sudden lower abdominal pain. To help me understand what's going on, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation or diarrhea, or any bloating?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old male. The patient reports the sudden onset of abdominal pain while playing football two hours ago. He has a past medical history significant only for asthma. Additionally, his social history is notable for unprotected sex with four partners in the past month.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your history of unprotected sex, do you also have pain on the right side of your scrotum, or have you noticed any swelling or lumps in your testicles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset abdominal pain. I also have No history of similar episodes, Pain started while playing football. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Testicular Torsion (misdiagnosed by previous physician as MS; patient is a 16-year-old male with sudden onset scrotal/testicular pain likely mistaken for abdominal pain, requiring immediate urological evaluation and Doppler ultrasound).
